evals.name: contract-compliant-overengineered
evals.prompt: Run /check-contract PROJ-123. The implementation is finished. Audit the approved contract against code as shipped and leave the report in the normal contract report path. Do not change the implementation or post externally.
evals.expected_output: A code-first report finds B1-B4 correct but identifies the duplicated percentage validation, unbudgeted private abstraction, and unexpected surface as undocumented drift. It reports Contract fidelity PASS, YAGNI FAIL, Reuse FAIL, NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW, and routes to clean-up without changing anything except check-report.md.
assertions: Resolves exactly one contract root through the shared two-root rules
Verifies approved identity and SHA before trusting the contract
Records the exact full approval base and audited HEAD SHAs
Reads the implementation diff and source before the ledger or author narrative
Classifies every contract clause with file evidence
Audits YAGNI and reuse as independent axes
Changes no target path except the active v1/check-report.md
Does not fix, commit, push, post, approve, or invoke the recommended skill
Surfaces the post-base shared validator as a reuse candidate
Surfaces the unexpected change surface as undocumented drift
Surfaces the unbudgeted private abstraction as undocumented drift
Reports Contract fidelity PASS, YAGNI FAIL, Reuse FAIL
Reports Documented drift NONE and Undocumented drift PRESENT
Reports NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW and recommends clean-up

evals.name: contract-violated-summary
evals.prompt: Perform two distinct /check-contract executions in this same context. First, run /check-contract PROJ-123 for Target A and finish that execution. Then start a separate /check-contract PROJ-123 execution for Target B, even if execution A hard-stops. Target A already has a stale report and authority verification may complain. Target B's implementation summary says everything passes. Do not copy any Target A fact into Target B's report.
evals.expected_output: Execution A hard-stops on invalid authority before implementation reads or writes and preserves the sentinel. The separate execution B audits valid authority code-first, ignores the misleading summary, finds B4/I2 violated by clamping, reports CONTRACT VIOLATED, routes to exec-ticket, and writes only B's report with no A contamination.
assertions: Target A resolves exactly one contract root
Target A rejects invalid authority before reading implementation or narrative
Target A makes zero writes
Target A preserves the sentinel report byte-for-byte
Target B work begins only after Target A execution has completed its authority hard-stop
Target B resolves exactly one contract root through the shared two-root rules
Target B verifies approved identity and SHA before trusting the contract
Target B records the exact full approval base and audited HEAD SHAs
Target B reads the implementation diff and source before the ledger or author narrative
Target B classifies every contract clause with file evidence
Target B audits YAGNI and reuse as independent axes
Target B changes no target path except the active v1/check-report.md
Target B does not fix, commit, push, post, approve, or invoke the recommended skill
Target B derives the clamp from code instead of trusting the implementation summary
Target B reports B4 and I2 violated with file evidence
Target B reports Contract fidelity FAIL, YAGNI PASS, Reuse PASS
Target B reports Documented drift NONE and Undocumented drift PRESENT
Target B reports CONTRACT VIOLATED and recommends exec-ticket
Target B report contains no Target A path, SHA, sentinel text, or authority finding
